issues.legal_issue: The standards of good cause and sufficient cause for explaining non-appearance do not materially differ.
material_facts: The defendant relied on the same alleged illness to explain his absence in applications seeking relief under the provisions governing participation after non-appearance and setting aside an ex parte decree.
issues.conclusion: There is no material difference between the facts required to satisfy the tests of good cause and sufficient cause for non-appearance.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order IX, rules 7 and 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court saw no material difference between good cause and sufficient cause as explanations for non-appearance. It observed that if there were a difference in degree of proof, failure to meet the lighter standard would also preclude meeting the higher one.

predicates.order_nine_nonappearance_applications: The proceeding involves applications seeking relief for a party's non-appearance at a civil hearing.
predicates.same_absence_ground: The party relies on the same explanation for absence in the successive applications.

issues.definition: When a party relies on the same explanation for absence in successive applications for non-appearance relief, the cause standards are materially equivalent.

issues.legal_issue: Res judicata can apply between stages of the same proceeding, but its application depends on the nature and scope of the earlier decision and the court's competence to make it.
material_facts: The disputed finding arose in an earlier stage of the same litigation and was relied on to bar consideration of the later application.
The court considered whether the earlier proceeding had finally determined the matter and whether the court was competent to decide it.
issues.conclusion: The principle of res judicata is not confined to section 11 and may apply between stages of the same proceeding, but it does not apply automatically to every interlocutory decision.
issues.legal_principle: The principle underlying section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure can apply to successive stages of the same litigation. Satyadhyan Ghosal v. Sm. Deorajin Debi was cited for that principle. The nature of the proceedings, the scope of the enquiry, applicable procedural provisions, and the first court's jurisdiction and competence must be considered; Satyadhyan Ghosal also distinguished interlocutory orders having the force of a decree from steps toward final adjudication.

predicates.same_proceeding_stages: The later matter arises at a subsequent stage of the same litigation.
predicates.competent_first_court: The court that considered the earlier matter had jurisdiction and competence to decide it.
predicates.prior_final_issue_determination: The earlier proceeding finally determined the same issue now raised again.

issues.definition: A matter finally determined by a competent court at an earlier stage of the same litigation bars its reconsideration at a later stage.

issues.legal_issue: A decision on an application to participate after an ex parte adjournment does not bar a later application to set aside an ex parte decree.
material_facts: The defendant first applied to undo the direction to proceed ex parte, and that application was rejected.
After an ex parte decree was entered, the defendant applied to set it aside on the same factual ground.
The earlier application was interlocutory and did not determine any issue in controversy in the suit or end the litigation.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision under Order IX, rule 7 did not operate as res judicata against the application under Order IX, rule 13, which had to be heard on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Order IX, rule 7 concerns orderly conduct of the suit and does not determine the merits or end the litigation; it provides no appeal from refusal to restore an earlier stage. Order IX, rule 13 supplies a specific remedy to set aside an ex parte decree. The Court referred to Sangram Singh v. Election Tribunal, Sankaralinga v. Ratnasabhapati, and Bhaoo Patel v. Naroo, and relied on the principle in Satyadhyan Ghosal that the character and effect of the earlier decision matter when res judicata is asserted between stages.

rule.if: civil_suit_nonappearance_proceeding and prior_rule_seven_application_decided and later_ex_parte_decree_application and earlier_decision_only_interlocutory

predicates.civil_suit_nonappearance_proceeding: The matter concerns a party's non-appearance during a civil suit.
predicates.prior_rule_seven_application_decided: The party earlier sought to re-enter the proceedings after the suit was directed to proceed in that party's absence, and the court decided that request.
predicates.later_ex_parte_decree_application: An ex parte decree was later entered and the party applied to have it set aside.
predicates.earlier_decision_only_interlocutory: The earlier decision regulated the progress of the suit without determining a disputed issue on the merits or ending the litigation.

issues.definition: When an interlocutory decision on re-entering a suit is followed by an application to set aside an ex parte decree, that application is heard on its merits without a res judicata bar.

issues.legal_issue: An application to restore a defendant to an earlier stage under Order IX, rule 7 is unavailable after the hearing is complete and the suit is adjourned only for pronouncement of judgment.
material_facts: The court had taken the plaintiff's evidence, completed the hearing, and reserved judgment.
The defendant applied to be restored to the earlier position after the hearing was complete and the suit stood only for pronouncement of judgment.
issues.conclusion: The court was not competent to entertain the application under Order IX, rule 7 at that stage; the matter proceeded under Order IX, rule 6, with Order IX, rule 13 available after the ex parte decree.
issues.legal_principle: Order IX, rule 7 applies where the court has adjourned the hearing of the suit ex parte and a hearing remains to take place. Where the hearing is complete and the court adjourns only to pronounce judgment under Order XX, rule 1, there is no adjournment for hearing; Order IX, rule 6 governs proceeding in the defendant's absence and Order IX, rule 13 provides the remedy after an ex parte decree.

rule.if: civil_suit_nonappearance_proceeding and hearing_completed and adjournment_only_for_judgment and later_stage_restoration_application

predicates.civil_suit_nonappearance_proceeding: The matter concerns a defendant's non-appearance during a civil suit.
predicates.hearing_completed: The court has completed the hearing, including the evidence taken for decision.
predicates.adjournment_only_for_judgment: The suit stands adjourned only so that judgment may be pronounced, with no further hearing remaining.
predicates.later_stage_restoration_application: The defendant applies to be restored to an earlier stage after the hearing has been completed.

issues.definition: A defendant who applies to return to an earlier stage after the hearing is complete and the suit is adjourned only for judgment has made an incompetent restoration application.

issues.legal_issue: The court's inherent powers cannot be used to provide a remedy for non-appearance where the procedural provisions exhaust the contingencies and remedies for that situation.
material_facts: The defendant sought to use the court's inherent power to obtain restoration to an earlier stage after the hearing was complete.
The procedural provisions addressed non-appearance during the suit and the setting aside of a resulting ex parte decree.
issues.conclusion: There was no scope to invoke inherent powers to entertain the application; the relevant procedural provisions exhausted the situations arising from a defendant's non-appearance.
issues.legal_principle: Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not permit inherent powers to override express or implied provisions of law. Where Order IX, rules 7 and 13 exhaust the contingencies concerning a defendant's non-appearance and the remedies available, inherent powers cannot be invoked to create an additional remedy.

predicates.civil_suit_nonappearance_proceeding: The matter concerns a defendant's non-appearance during a civil suit.
predicates.procedural_remedies_exhaust_nonappearanc: The procedural scheme provides for the relevant situations arising from the defendant's non-appearance and the remedies available for them.
predicates.requested_relief_outside_provided_remedi: The party requests a remedy that is not available under the procedural provisions governing those situations.

issues.definition: Where procedural remedies exhaust the contingencies arising from non-appearance, inherent power cannot supply a further remedy outside them.

issues.legal_issue: A decision on a request for relief in one jointly tried suit does not, merely because the suits were tried together, bar a separate request for relief in another suit.
material_facts: Several suits were ordered to be tried jointly, with evidence in the main suit treated as evidence in the connected suits.
An application seeking restoration of a dismissed suit was decided separately from the later application to set aside an ex parte decree in another suit.
The applications concerned relief specific to their respective suits, although they relied on similar facts.
issues.conclusion: The decision in the restoration application for one suit did not operate as res judicata against the application to set aside the ex parte decree in the other suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11's res judicata principle requires identity of the matter decided and does not make a decision on an application in one suit binding in another merely because the suits were consolidated or tried jointly. Each suit's relief and the issue arising under the applicable provision must be considered separately.

predicates.separate_civil_suits_jointly_tried: Distinct suits are directed to be tried together or share evidence.
predicates.relief_specific_to_each_suit: The applications seek remedies that arise separately in their respective suits.
predicates.decision_in_one_suit_invoked_against_app: A party relies on a decision in one suit to bar an application in a different suit.

issues.definition: Joint trial does not make a decision on suit-specific relief in one suit a bar to an application for separate relief in another suit.

issues.legal_issue: A decree entered after a suit is directed to proceed ex parte is not a merits decree under the provision for failure to perform an act for which time was granted unless that provision's conditions are met.
material_facts: The defendant was absent when the suit was called for hearing, and the court directed that it proceed ex parte.
The hearing was completed and the decree was expressly treated as ex parte throughout the proceedings.
The adjournment had followed a joint request concerning a possible compromise, not a grant of time to the defendant alone to perform an act necessary for further progress of the suit.
issues.conclusion: The requirements for a merits decision under Order XVII, rule 3 were not met, and the decree was an ex parte decree that could be challenged under Order IX, rule 13.
issues.legal_principle: Order XVII, rule 3 applies where a party to whom time has been granted fails to produce evidence, procure witnesses, or perform another act necessary to the further progress of the suit for which time was allowed. On the facts, that condition was absent; the court and parties treated the proceedings as ex parte, so Order IX, rule 13 applied.

rule.if: civil_suit_nonappearance_proceeding and defendant_absent_at_hearing and court_proceeds_ex_parte and not party_granted_time_for_required_act

predicates.civil_suit_nonappearance_proceeding: The matter concerns a party's participation in a civil suit.
predicates.defendant_absent_at_hearing: The defendant does not appear when the suit is called for hearing.
predicates.court_proceeds_ex_parte: The court records that the suit will proceed in the defendant's absence.
predicates.party_granted_time_for_required_act: The defendant was granted time to perform an act necessary to the further progress of the suit and failed to perform it.

issues.definition: When a defendant is absent, the court proceeds ex parte, and the defendant was not granted time to perform a required act, the resulting decree is ex parte rather than a merits decree.
